prompt: What does the passage say about supernatural mentality and the Holy Spirit?

options.text: It is impossible and cannot be operated without the ministry of the Holy Spirit, who reveals and co-ordinates its operation inside you
It is possible without Him but far slower
It belongs to those who have received a special calling
It is available only to those in full-time ministry

explanation: The claim is absolute, and the chapter repeats it: there is no substitute for the ministry of the Holy Spirit in the school of divine wisdom or supernatural mentality.

why.a: Correct. Impossible without Him, and He both reveals and co-ordinates its operation.
why.b: Wrong. Slower would make Him optional, and the passage says impossible.
why.c: Wrong. No special calling is required; the chapter addresses every reader.
why.d: Wrong. The book's examples are businessmen and workers as much as ministers.

prompt: How does the passage describe what the Holy Spirit does with your mentality?

options.text: He sits upon it, collates facts for you and delivers them in concrete terms, so you have no doubt why you are taking the step He tells you to take
He overrides your thinking and acts in your place
He gives impressions that must be tested by others
He quiets the mind so that it stops working

explanation: Collates is the operative verb. It preserves the book's consistent position that the Spirit works WITH the mind rather than instead of it.

why.a: Correct. Sitting upon your mentality, collating facts and delivering them concretely.
why.b: Wrong. Chapter 2 says explicitly that God will not think for you.
why.c: Wrong. Testing by others is not mentioned; the delivery is said to be concrete enough to remove doubt.
why.d: Wrong. The book wants the mind more active, not less.

topic: the Spirit at work in four men
prompt: In whom does this chapter say the Holy Spirit was at work?

options.text: Joseph, Daniel, Peter and Stephen
Joseph, Daniel and Peter
Moses, Joshua and Stephen
Paul, Peter, James and John

explanation: Chapter 10 gives the four-name version. Chapter 3 gave three, Joseph, Daniel and Peter, so Stephen is the addition here, and Acts 6:10 backs it: they could not resist the spirit and wisdom with which Stephen spoke.

why.a: Correct. Four names in this chapter, with Stephen added.
why.b: Wrong, and it is a close call, because that IS the list, but in Chapter 3.
why.c: Wrong. Moses and Joshua appear in this chapter only for the laying on of hands in Numbers 27:18.
why.d: Wrong. Peter, James and John are the three in the imagination illustration in Chapter 2.

prompt: Which scripture speaks of the manifold wisdom of God that disarms principalities and powers?

options.text: Ephesians 3:10
Ephesians 4:23
Ephesians 1:17-18
Colossians 2:3

explanation: Ephesians 3:10. The manifold wisdom of God is said to put you in natural command of the forces of darkness, with them in subjection.

why.a: Correct. Ephesians 3:10 is the manifold wisdom verse.
why.b: Wrong. Ephesians 4:23 is 'be renewed in the spirit of your mind', from Chapter 1.
why.c: Wrong. Ephesians 1:17-18 is Paul's prayer for the spirit of wisdom and revelation, from Chapter 2.
why.d: Wrong. Colossians 2:3 is the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hid in Christ, quoted later in this same chapter.

prompt: According to John 14:26 and John 16:13 as cited, what will the Holy Spirit do?

options.text: Teach us all things, and show us things to come
Convict the world of sin, and glorify Christ
Bear witness with our spirit, and help our infirmities
Give gifts to every man severally as He will

explanation: Two verses, two functions, and the conclusion drawn is that He takes things from God and passes them to you, becoming your medium of connection to supernatural intelligence.

why.a: Correct. Teach all things from 14:26, show things to come from 16:13.
why.b: Wrong. A genuine work of the Spirit from John 16 that this book does not cite.
why.c: Wrong. Those are Romans 8 phrases the book does not use.
why.d: Wrong. That is 1 Corinthians 12 and does not appear here.

prompt: What four things does the passage say the treasure of wisdom and knowledge gives you?

options.text: Insight, foresight, dominion and unequaled creativity
Long life, riches, pleasantness and happiness
Wisdom, counsel, knowledge and understanding
Power, love, a sound mind and boldness

explanation: Cited to Job 28:7-28. The Holy Spirit is called your principal access into that treasure, which is hid in Christ per Colossians 2:3.

why.a: Correct. These four are the ones named here.
why.b: Wrong. That is the summary list of the products of divine wisdom in Chapter 5.
why.c: Wrong. That is what the Holy Ghost Himself is called in Chapter 3.
why.d: Wrong. Power, love and a sound mind are from 2 Timothy 1:7 in Chapter 5, and boldness is not in that list.

prompt: According to Numbers 27:18 as cited, what happened when Moses laid his hands on Joshua?

options.text: He was filled with the spirit of wisdom
He received the mantle of prophecy
He was made judge over Israel
He received power to divide the Jordan

explanation: The application is direct: you too can be filled with wisdom. It is the only laying on of hands mentioned in the book, apart from Paul's charge to Timothy in 2 Timothy 1:6.

why.a: Correct. Filled with the spirit of wisdom, which is why the example appears in a chapter about mental revolution.
why.b: Wrong. Prophecy is not what the verse names.
why.c: Wrong. The judges are not discussed in this book.
why.d: Wrong. The Jordan is not mentioned anywhere.

prompt: How does this chapter describe Peter's Pentecost delivery?

options.text: Without opening any book he blasted the whole city with an irresistible message of redemption, and 3,000 souls got saved the same hour
He read from the prophets and expounded them for an hour
He spoke briefly and the apostles finished the work
He preached for three days before the city responded

explanation: Chapter 3 gave the same event as thirty minutes and 3,000 converts. Here the emphasis is that he opened no book, which is what makes it evidence of supernatural intelligence rather than preparation.

why.a: Correct. No book opened, the whole city, 3,000 souls, the same hour.
why.b: Wrong. Reading would undercut the point, and the passage says he opened no book.
why.c: Wrong. The delivery is credited entirely to Peter.
why.d: Wrong. It was the same hour, and Chapter 3 says thirty minutes.

prompt: What does the passage say yielding to the Holy Spirit will take you beyond?

options.text: Beyond speaking in tongues and laying hands on the sick, to a place of astounding mental exploits
Beyond the reach of every enemy
Beyond the need for further learning
Beyond the ordinary duties of church life

explanation: It names two familiar charismatic practices and puts mental exploits above them, which is the book's central re-ordering of priorities.

why.a: Correct. Tongues and laying hands on the sick are the two named, and mental exploits is the destination.
why.b: Wrong. Chapter 9 says every great door commands adversaries, so escape from enemies is not promised.
why.c: Wrong. Chapter 8 makes research a permanent duty.
why.d: Wrong. Church duties are not the comparison being made.

prompt: What does the passage say the Holy Spirit's nature as the Excellent Spirit points to?

options.text: His mission, which is to supernaturally generate excellence in the believer
His equality with the Father and the Son
His preference for those who are already diligent
His role as the judge of every work

explanation: He is called the Excellent Spirit in Daniel chapter 6, and He introduces supernatural order to your mental faculty, so you can coordinate things naturally beyond your intellectual capacity.

why.a: Correct. Nature points to mission, and the mission is to generate excellence in the believer.
why.b: Wrong. Doctrinal relations within the Trinity are never discussed.
why.c: Wrong. No preference for the already diligent is stated.
why.d: Wrong. Judgment is not a role assigned to Him here.

prompt: What does the passage say about today and tomorrow?

options.text: Where you are now is not good enough for tomorrow; today is just good enough for today, and you must prepare today for what will be enough for tomorrow
Tomorrow will take care of itself if today is well spent
What served yesterday will serve again if it is applied faithfully
Tomorrow's grace is given only when tomorrow comes

explanation: Relevance requires constant fresh filling. Chapter 9 says the same thing under the pride of past achievements: where you are today may look amazing, but it is not good enough for tomorrow.

why.a: Correct. All three clauses are given, and the demand is preparation now.
why.b: Wrong. This is a real proverb the book does not use, and it counsels the passivity the book attacks.
why.c: Wrong. This is precisely what the Benin building story disproves.
why.d: Wrong. Grace is required for inspiration in Chapter 6, but this passage is about preparing in advance.

prompt: Who pointed out the building in Benin that had lost relevance?

options.text: Archbishop Benson Idahosa
Bishop Abioye
Dr. Frederick K. C. Price
David Yonggi Cho

explanation: They were riding in a car together in Benin when he pointed it out. It was a bungalow with a balcony in front, and it had been the best in Benin many years earlier.

why.a: Correct. Archbishop Benson Idahosa is the one who told the story.
why.b: Wrong. Bishop Abioye recommended Dynamics Of Holiness in the testimony in Chapter 8.
why.c: Wrong. Dr. Frederick K. C. Price showed the author around his office, in Chapter 8.
why.d: Wrong. David Yonggi Cho appears for his wife's books and his large congregation.

prompt: What had become of the Benin building by the time the story was told?

options.text: If the government were to reconstruct the road they would not think twice about pulling it down
It had been sold and turned into a church
It had been rebuilt to a higher standard
It had been abandoned and overgrown

explanation: The owner had lived in London, would come home in December and stand on the balcony waving to passers-by, and everybody would marvel 'Ah! What a house!' The building had simply lost relevance.

why.a: Correct. The road reconstruction line is how the story lands, and the verdict is that it had lost relevance.
why.b: Wrong. No change of use is mentioned.
why.c: Wrong. Rebuilding would defeat the point of the illustration.
why.d: Wrong. Abandonment is not stated; irrelevance is, which is subtler and worse.

prompt: What does the passage say you become when the Spirit rests on your mentality?

options.text: A man of sweatless triumph and dignity among men
A man of unshakeable conviction
A man whose words carry weight
A man free from every earthly care

explanation: Sweatless triumph is the book's own phrase, and it fits its whole argument that insight outperforms struggle. It is preceded by the reminder that it is not possible by might or power but by the enabling of the Spirit of God.

why.a: Correct. Sweatless triumph and dignity among men is the phrase as printed.
why.b: Wrong. Conviction is used to define belief in Chapter 1, not here.
why.c: Wrong. A plausible phrase the book does not use at this point.
why.d: Wrong. Freedom from care is close to the peace wisdom brings in Chapter 5, but not this sentence.

prompt: How does the final chapter describe the mind you possess?

options.text: A unique mind, redeemed, regenerated and anointed, the mind of Christ, a sound mind
A mind under construction that will be complete in eternity
A mind equal to any other, made effective by discipline
A mind that must be guarded because it is fragile

explanation: The chapter opens with the summary and adds that it has what it takes to produce sound results and amazing mental exploits.

why.a: Correct. All five descriptions are stacked in the opening sentence.
why.b: Wrong. Chapter 1 says it was delivered as a COMPLETE package at new birth.
why.c: Wrong. Discipline matters, but the chapter's claim is that the mind itself is unique.
why.d: Wrong. Guarding the mind is taught in Chapter 2, but fragility is not the description here.

prompt: What does the final chapter say about the brains that will humble the intellectual world?

options.text: They are being birthed right now, and you are one of them
They will arise in a future generation
They are hidden and will be revealed at the end
They have already appeared and should be followed

explanation: The reader is told to convince himself that he is one of them, and that they will leave an indelible mark on this new millennium.

why.a: Correct. Being birthed right now, and the reader is included directly.
why.b: Wrong. A future generation would remove the personal address the passage insists on.
why.c: Wrong. Concealment is not part of the claim.
why.d: Wrong. The reader is one of them, not a follower of them.

prompt: Which psalm does the final chapter say God is fulfilling in our midst?

options.text: Psalm 87, that all the springs of life are in Zion
Psalm 92, that even in old age they shall bring forth fruit
Psalm 119, on meditation all the day
Psalm 24, that the earth is the Lord's

explanation: Psalm 87 and the springs of life in Zion. The book cites several psalms and each does a different job, so the reference matters.

why.a: Correct. Psalm 87 is cited here, for the springs of life being in Zion.
why.b: Wrong. Psalm 92:14 is cited in Chapters 8 and 9, on fruit in old age.
why.c: Wrong. Psalm 119:96-100 is David's meditation passage in Chapter 2.
why.d: Wrong. Psalm 24:1 is quoted in Chapter 5 under wealth.

prompt: What does the author prophesy over the reader's mental faculty at the close of the book?

options.text: That the wind of God infuse fresh life, that the fire of the Holy Ghost burn off every chaff, and that there be a supernatural refining of the mental system
That every evil imagination be cast down and every stronghold pulled down
That the reader receive the gift of wisdom and the gift of knowledge
That the reader be filled afresh with the Holy Ghost every morning

explanation: Three prophecies in a row, plus a fourth, that of your supernatural rising. The imagery of wind and dry bones runs through the passage.

why.a: Correct. Wind, fire burning off chaff, and supernatural refining are the three named.
why.b: Wrong. Casting down imaginations belongs to Chapter 2, from 2 Corinthians 10.
why.c: Wrong. Spiritual gifts of that kind are never listed in this book.
why.d: Wrong. Being constantly filled afresh is Chapter 10's counsel, not one of these prophecies.

prompt: What happened after the one insight the author received about the all-night meetings?

options.text: The gathering went from about fifteen people to 3,000 at the next meeting
The meetings were moved to a larger hall
The gathering doubled every month for a year
The meetings were discontinued and replaced

explanation: Fifteen to three thousand, on the strength of a single insight. Note that 3,000 also appears twice for Peter's converts at Pentecost, so keep the two uses apart.

why.a: Correct. About fifteen people, then 3,000 at the next meeting.
why.b: Wrong. Venue is not mentioned; the growth is the point.
why.c: Wrong. Gradual growth would defeat the claim, which is that ONE insight did it at once.
why.d: Wrong. The meetings continued and grew.

prompt: What does the closing passage say one striking supernatural insight is enough to do?

options.text: Bring a man into the limelight, release him from prison and plant him in the palace, set a colourful order back in your destiny, and make a millionaire of any pauper
Settle every question you have ever asked
Secure your family for three generations
Remove every adversary from your path

explanation: Four claims in one sentence. The prison to palace image echoes Joseph, announced in the palace while still in prison, and Peter in Chapter 3.

why.a: Correct. All four are listed, and the millionaire and pauper pairing closes it.
why.b: Wrong. Answers are a product of wisdom in Chapter 5, but this is not that claim.
why.c: Wrong. Generations are not mentioned.
why.d: Wrong. Chapter 9 says every great door commands the attention of adversaries.

topic: your place will not be lost
prompt: What does the final chapter say about your place?

options.text: It is now up to individuals to begin to take their places, and your place will not be lost to another
Your place must be contended for against rivals
Your place will be given to another if you delay too long
Your place is revealed only after long obedience

explanation: It answers Chapter 3's warning that until you are empowered your place is not guaranteed, with the assurance that the place itself is not transferable.

why.a: Correct. Both halves are given, and the assurance is that it will not be lost to another.
why.b: Wrong. Rivalry is not part of the picture, and comparison is condemned as an obstacle.
why.c: Wrong. This directly contradicts the sentence.
why.d: Wrong. Obedience is a condition elsewhere, but this passage is about the place being reserved.

prompt: Fill the blank: "One striking supernatural insight is worth more in value than a {{1}} of struggles."
explanation: Lifetime. The line appears twice in the book, at the end of Chapter 5 and again in the closing paragraph, which makes it the single most repeated summary of its thesis.

prompt: Which passage is quoted at length as the ground for the Holy Spirit revealing the deep things of God?

options.text: 1 Corinthians 2:6-13
1 Corinthians 4:20
1 Corinthians 16:9
1 Corinthians 8:2

explanation: It includes 'Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him', and that the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.

why.a: Correct. 1 Corinthians 2:6-13 is the long quotation opening this chapter.
why.b: Wrong. 1 Corinthians 4:20 is the kingdom in power, from Chapter 3.
why.c: Wrong. 1 Corinthians 16:9 is the great door and many adversaries, from Chapter 9.
why.d: Wrong. 1 Corinthians 8:2 is on thinking you know something, from Chapter 8.

prompt: The passage says it is enough simply to know that the Holy Spirit is available.

options.text: True
False

explanation: False. 'It is one thing to know that the Holy Spirit is available, it's another thing to know how to gain access into His ministry.' You have to embrace His ministry before you can operate in that realm.

why.true: Wrong. Availability and access are explicitly distinguished.
why.false: Correct. Knowing the instrument of access matters as much as knowing it exists, which is why the chapter names the Holy Spirit as the gateway.

prompt: Which image does the final chapter use for what is rising as the wind blows?

options.text: Out of the once-upon-a-time valley of dry bones, a mighty host is rising to their feet
Out of the ashes, a phoenix is rising
Out of the wilderness, a highway is appearing
Out of the deep, a new creation is forming

explanation: The dry bones image is paired with the giants of the new millennium rising, and with the prophecy that the wind of God infuse fresh life into whatever appears dead in your life.

why.a: Correct. The valley of dry bones and the mighty host rising to their feet.
why.b: Wrong. The phoenix is not a biblical image and does not appear.
why.c: Wrong. A way in the wilderness is genuinely quoted from Isaiah 43:19, but in Chapter 9 and for a different purpose.
why.d: Wrong. The deep appears in the creation and inspiration passages, not here.
